newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom traffic rises 36 pct in Q4.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom traffic rises 36 pct in Q4.

text.p: Long distance telephone company WorldCom Inc on Thursday said it produced very strong performance for the fourth quarter of 1996 with traffic carried rising 36 percent from a year earlier.
For the year traffic rose 25 percent. Both figures exclude the effcts of the $14 billion acquisition of MFS Communications Co Inc in August.

"We continue to lead the industry in financial performance," said chief executive Bernard Ebbers. "The rapidly changing regulatory and technological environment have created unprecedented opportunities to further this growth."
Net income, excluding the MFS merger-related charges of $2.26 billion, increased to $119.7 million, or $0.29 per share, from $79.1 million, or $0.20 per share, for the fourth quarter of 1995.
This beat the First Call analysts' consensus estimate of $0.27 per share.
The stock opened 3/8 higher at 27-1/2 on Nasdaq.
Including charges, WorldCom lost $5.22 per share, or a total of $2.14 billion, in the fourth quarter, against a profit of $0.20 per share, or $79.1 million, in the year-ago period.

The fourth quarter showed a 31 percent rise in private line and frame relay services from a year earlier, a 35 percent increase in switched wholesale and commercial traffic, and a 29 percent rise in wholesale and commercial revenues.

MFS stand-alone fourth quarter revenue was $391.0 million, compared with $171.1 million a year ago. The increase was due in part to MFS's takeover of Internet service provider UUNET plus gains in international and telecom segments.
For all 1996, MFS revenue was $1.12 billion, up from $583.2 million for 1995.
